claim: Try it with sample data loads a seeded replay capsule without saving browser data.
sandbox: fresh browser context; enter /demo from the landing page, assert sample data and empty storage, reset, then exit

claim: The library makes no network calls; the demo uses only same-origin static files and no API, analytics, or third-party runtime service.
where: landing facts, demo telemetry, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh /demo load and replay; record every request and assert every URL is same-origin

claim: Recording begins only after the person starts it.
sandbox: fresh /demo; send game input before and after Arm & start and compare the captured-event count

claim: Text fields and editable elements are never captured, including controls inside open or closed Shadow DOM.
sandbox: fresh /demo recording; type in light DOM, editable, open-shadow, and closed-shadow controls; download and assert zero events

claim: The demo records timed keyboard input with a seed, downloads JSON, imports it, and replays the same event sequence.
where: landing headline and demo, README overview
sandbox: fresh demo; record four key events, download the capsule, import that file, replay, and assert completion

claim: The recorder stores a developer-supplied seed, timed input, and JSON-safe checkpoints only after start.
where: landing capture flow, demo captured fields, README overview
sandbox: new recorder with a controlled clock; assert pre-start exclusion and the exact exported seed, key event, timing, and checkpoint

claim: The recorder uses a 128 KB default cap and stops before it crosses that cap.
sandbox: new recorder with default options; append an oversized JSON checkpoint and measure the final serialized capsule

claim: Custom recorder and import caps support the full 4 KB–1 MB range.
sandbox: construct recorders at 4096, 128000, and 1000000 bytes; reject lower, higher, and fractional values

claim: Imported capsules are schema-validated and reject malformed, unsupported, or over-limit files.
sandbox: validate malformed JSON, unsupported versions, over-limit input, and invalid checkpoint labels

claim: Pointer coordinates are normalized to the configured target.
where: demo captured fields, privacy page, README
sandbox: dispatch a pointer event at 20% × 80% of the canvas, download the capsule, and assert x=0.2 and y=0.8

claim: Gamepads are sampled once per animation frame; changed samples use observation time and retain a finite browser timestamp as diagnostic metadata.
where: demo captured fields, privacy page, README
sandbox: stub requestAnimationFrame and getGamepads; assert one event per changed sample, observation time, and rounded browser timestamp

claim: Replay emits normalized events and checkpoints through callbacks in timestamp order.
where: landing adapter explanation, README replay API
sandbox: play a mixed event and checkpoint capsule and assert callback order

claim: The public player can pause, resume, stop, and accelerate replay.
sandbox: new player with speed 100; play, pause, resume, stop, and observe each state

claim: The Phaser fixture reproduces at least 90% of 20 seeded failures.
sandbox: import 20 generated replay capsules into the shipped deterministic Phaser model and count reproduced faults

claim: The package exports working ESM, CommonJS, and TypeScript declarations.
sandbox: build the library, load both module formats, and inspect the emitted declaration surface

claim: The hosted release artifact installs in a fresh npm project and works through both import and require.
sandbox: install the shipped versioned tarball into an empty temporary project and execute ESM and CommonJS consumers

claim: The package has zero runtime dependencies.
sandbox: read package.json and assert that the runtime dependencies object is empty

claim: The demo continues to record after its first load when the browser is offline.
sandbox: new browser context; load /demo, set only that context offline, start recording, and assert a new event is captured

claim: Replay Capsule is free, open-source software under the MIT License.
sandbox: assert package.json declares MIT and the shipped LICENSE contains the MIT License text
